Comments:
Q4 performance has improved compared to Q3, increasing to an average of 76.8% from 69.8%, reflecting continued progress in stabilising reactive emergency service delivery.
The introduction and embedding of a reviewed mitigation process for Business Critical events has supported improved management and visibility of reactive tasks. As in Q3, performance continues to be impacted primarily by system and process-related factors, particularly around security and fire alarm task closures, rather than service delivery capability.

There remains some inconsistency in the interpretation of Business Critical definitions between parties; however, this is being progressed through Contract Management Board governance, with further clarification and communication issued during the quarter.

In parallel, a focused backlog closure activity has been in progress throughout the next quarter, targeting historic reactive tasks to improve overall SLA performance and system accuracy.

Overall, whilst performance variability remains at a monthly level, the overall quarterly position demonstrates a clear improving trend, supported by strengthened controls and governance.

KPI name and description: Planned Maintenance Statutory (PMS) Completion - Monthly completion rate of statutory maintenance tasks.
Comments:

Performance improvements continue to be underpinned by sustained focus on asset data cleansing and taxonomy alignment, which remain key enablers to driving accuracy and consistency across the CAFM system. The statutory PPM mitigation process remains embedded and is being actively managed through Working Day 8 governance, alongside regular operational cadence calls to reinforce compliance and housekeeping standards.

Whilst there is a slight month-on-month decline towards the end of the quarter, this reflects the continued impact of legacy backlog positions. A targeted backlog reduction plan has been implemented, through the next quarter, addressing both PPM completion and supporting activity to increase improvement in forward performance.

Overall, with the controls now in place expected to drive a more consistent upward trend into 2026.

Q4 saw an increase in reported complaints, with an average of 8 compared to 6 in Q3, reflecting a notable change in reporting levels.

This uplift should be considered in the context of a new complaints process introduced within Defra Group Property (DgP), which has driven increased visibility and capture of issues. A collaborative approach has been taken, identifying that there were issues with the current process. This has now been reviewed and is due to be fully rolled out over the next quarter, this is also about using the mitigation process correctly through the Working Day 8 process.

Seasonal impacts, including the December holiday period and increased annual leave, also contributed to fluctuations in service delivery and complaint volumes during the quarter.
Encouragingly, there has been continued collaboration with Defra stakeholders, including the delivery of a joint workshop with the Defra SLT, providing transparency on cleaning methodologies and contractual outputs. This supports improved understanding of service delivery expectations and helps address perception-based complaints.

A more structured and aligned complaints management process is in progress and expected to be rolled out, which will support improved consistency in how complaints are managed, reported, and closed.

Overall, whilst complaint volumes have increased, this is reflective of improved reporting mechanisms showing full visibility of complaints, to allow trend analysis, along with complaints being validated through an agreed process in the Working Day 8 mitigation call.
